A shallower network tolerates a large learning rate better, as in experiment 60.
Wider layers amplify the update magnitude at high learning rates and cause divergence, as in experiment 86.
With small learning rates there is no instability risk, and extra depth adds capacity, as in experiments 46 and 43.
Wider layers speed up learning when the step size is small, as in experiment 83.
